reason: The front of the arm needs bone mineral, and the picture shows its bone tissue awaiting it.
expectation: The mineral should strengthen the bone at the biceps attachment.

alternatives.reason: The muscle cells also appear intended for the front, but either order is allowed.

effect: Mineral is now in the front bone; the biceps still needs to be built.
reaction: The picture makes it clear that the mineral strengthens bone without hardening the tendons.
reason: The front still has a space for the biceps, and the muscle cells are the available material for building it.
expectation: The muscle cells should form the biceps at the front of the arm.

effect: The front is complete: the biceps pulls through its tendon to bend the elbow, with the mineralized bone carrying the pull.
reaction: The pull demonstration makes the connection between muscle and bone clearer.
reason: The back bone also has a named mineral slot, so I can strengthen the triceps attachment the same way.
expectation: The mineral should strengthen the bone at the back attachment.

alternatives.reason: I could build the triceps first; the introduction says either order works.

effect: The back bone is mineralized, leaving the triceps to build.
reaction: This matches the front and keeps the tendons and joint soft.
reason: The back still needs its triceps, and muscle cells built the biceps on the front.
expectation: The cells should form the triceps and complete the back attachment.

effect: The back is complete. The triceps demonstration shows how pulling behind the elbow straightens the arm, unlike the biceps pull at the front.
reaction: It was satisfying to compare how the same kind of muscle cells can produce opposite movements.

mostWorthwhile.text: Building the biceps was most worthwhile because the demonstration showed how its tendon carries the pull to the bone and bends the elbow.

leastWorthwhile.text: Adding mineral to the back felt repetitive after doing the same thing at the front, even though it completed the other attachment.

surprise.text: The same kind of muscle cells could straighten the elbow at the back and bend it at the front because of where they attach.

arbitrary.text: No action felt particularly arbitrary: the named slots and pictures made the muscle and mineral placements clear.

continue.text: I would choose to continue for another chapter to see more demonstrations connecting body structures to what they do, though I hope the next build is less repetitive.
